label: PF Backlog 578
title: Eventing SSOT (Go): event core - append-only store, emit, monotonic seq, cursor/since
body:
## Problem / why
The canonical stream has no reliable cursor (since = string timestamp compare) and no Go-native core; new
shipped logic must be Go.

## Goal / value
A Go event core owning emit + append-only store + monotonic seq + cursor reads; single writer.

## In scope
- Go package (extend go/pfcore or new go/eventbus) with emit/seq/cursor; single-writer store.
- Invoked from Python via core/go_host + A1 wire (fail-closed).

## Out of scope
- Dispatch/transports (E4/E5); changing existing Python emit call sites (E7).

## Acceptance criteria
- Monotonic seq assigned; cursor read returns exactly events after a cursor (no races).
- Existing events.jsonl readers still work; no duplicate store introduced.

## Verification / test plan
- Go unit tests + Python contract/e2e test; language_rule_check green.

decisions.decision: Add event append/read ops to go/pfcore via the A1 wire; Python stays writer until 1272; portable lockfile for append+seq

prior_decisions: ADR-0005: Go core owns store+emit+seq+cursor; Python thin client; single writer; A1 seam; extend go/pfcore first (Q1)
BI-PF-1267: event-envelope contract (schema) defined; wire-request op enum = ping/describe/validate/canonicalize
core/events.py:1-11 is the single writer of events.jsonl (Python) until the 1272 cutover (Q4)
core/go_host.py: stateless one-shot subprocess seam (stdin/stdout), fail-closed, builds the binary on demand
ADR-0001: new shipped/sensitive logic -> Go under go/; no new Python modules in core/
existing_path: Go host + op dispatch -> go/pfcore/pfcore.go Handle; main.go reads one wire-request
wire contract + op enum -> core/contracts.py (_WIRE_REQUEST) + go/contract + go/pfcore mirrors
event store (SSOT) -> products/<project>/events.jsonl via core/events.py + core/log_router
portable exclusive lock pattern -> core/worker.py:84-105 (O_CREAT|O_EXCL lockfile)
invocation -> core/go_host.invoke(op, contract_name, payload, req_id, source)
assumptions: C1 event ops are added to go/pfcore (not a separate binary) by extending the wire-request op enum (additive)
C2 the stateless Go core receives the store path in the payload (it does not know ROOT)
C3 during 1268 Python REMAINS the writer (no dual write); Go ops are exercised by tests + available via go_host; the emit-path cutover is 1272
C4 portable exclusive lock (O_CREATE|O_EXCL lockfile, mirroring core/worker) for append+seq; stdlib-only Go (no new deps)
C5 monotonic seq = last persisted seq + 1 under the lock (sidecar counter only if needed)
divergences: extending the frozen wire-request op enum is a contract change -> recorded as a decision (additive; both Go mirrors + parity test)
a Go writer alongside the Python writer would break single-writer -> explicitly avoided until the 1272 cutover
open_questions: Q1 op shape: discrete ops (event_append/event_read) vs one 'events' op with an action field
Q2 wiring for 1268: ops exercised by tests + reachable via go_host (dormant on the emit path) vs feature-flagged call
Q3 seq source: last-line+1 vs a sidecar counter file
Q4 store scope/path passed by the caller (product_forge root vs product dir)
Q5 ownership: 1268 builds+exposes the core; the Python cutover stays 1272 (no overlap)
